skill.name: review
skill.description: Reviews repository changes against a chosen git reference, then separates standards issues from spec mismatches using parallel sub-agents.
skill.summary: Reviews a git diff against repository standards and the originating spec.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code backticks around filenames, headings, and examples. One external command instruction is confirmed because the skill tells the agent to run git diff and git log, and a semantic finding notes that the user-supplied fixed point should not be passed through without validation.

remediation.issue: User-supplied git ref is inserted into command examples.
remediation.suggestion: Require validation of the fixed point as a git revision and tell agents to pass it as a separate argument, not through shell interpolation.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes Against Standards and Specs
content.value_statement: Code changes can follow style rules but still miss the requested behavior. This skill compares a diff against repo standards and a source spec in separate reviews.
actual_capabilities: Compares HEAD with a user-selected commit, branch, tag, or merge-base.
Uses git diff and git log commands to define the review scope.
Searches for issue, PRD, or spec sources that describe the intended change.
Collects repository standards from common documentation and config files.
Runs standards and spec checks as separate sub-agent reviews.
Reports findings under separate Standards and Spec sections.
limitations: Requires a valid fixed point before the review can start.
Spec review is skipped or limited when no issue, PRD, or spec is available.
It does not run project test suites or linters by itself.
It depends on accessible repository files and issue tracker configuration.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Readiness
use_cases.description: Check a branch against main before requesting review, with standards and spec issues separated.

use_cases.title: Spec Compliance Review
use_cases.description: Compare implementation details with an issue, PRD, or spec before delivery.

use_cases.title: Standards Enforcement
use_cases.description: Find places where a change conflicts with documented team conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Against Main
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a current branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current branch against main using the review skill.

prompt_templates.title: Review Since Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a known range of committed work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review changes since commit <commit_sha>. Use the issue or PRD referenced by the commits when available.

prompt_templates.title: Review With Spec Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Review when the spec source is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this branch against origin/main. Use specs/payments-redesign.md as the spec source.

prompt_templates.title: Review Release Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review release/candidate against v2.4.0. Separate documented standards violations from spec gaps, and keep the axes independent.

output_examples.output: Standards review reports one missing architecture note. Spec review reports no missing requirement. Summary lists one standards finding and zero spec findings.

output_examples.input: Review against origin/main using the checkout spec.
output_examples.output: Standards review finds no documented violations. Spec review identifies a missing refund requirement and one behavior outside the requested scope.

output_examples.input: Review since v1.8.0 with no available spec.
output_examples.output: Standards review lists two convention issues. Spec review is skipped because no issue, PRD, or spec was available.

best_practices: Provide the fixed point and spec path when you know them.
Keep repository standards documents current and easy to find.
Review the two result sections independently before prioritizing work.
anti_patterns: Using the skill without a fixed point.
Treating the spec review as a substitute for tests.
Merging the two review axes into one ranked list.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews changes between HEAD and a fixed point for standards violations and spec mismatches.

faq.question: Does it require a spec?
faq.answer: No. If no spec is available, the Spec section should say that it was skipped.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute tests?
faq.answer: No. It reviews diffs and documents. Run tests separately when needed.

faq.question: Can it review work in progress?
faq.answer: It is best for committed branch work because the process compares HEAD against a fixed point.

faq.question: Why are Standards and Spec separated?
faq.answer: A change can satisfy one axis and fail the other. Separate reports make that visible.
